ana: quick q — operator UX for routing/quota config: should admin/control APIs be gRPC or REST+JSON? Console team needs easy incremental updates and live reflect of rules.

mike: +1 to thinking about client ergonomics. gRPC gives streaming for live updates but adding clients for every internal tool might be friction.

jess: Console cares about simple fetch endpoints and predictable error messages. JSON is easier for ad-hoc debugging (curl, network tab). But streaming would be nice for the live rule editor.

tom: For quotas/rollouts we also need reliable metrics hooks. gRPC metadata can carry traces easily, but we already have middleware that injects trace headers for HTTP.

mike: Practical tradeoff: do gRPC for the control plane but provide a small JSON gateway for the Console and web UIs. That avoids shipping browser gRPC clients.

ana: @mike spelling — ana :)

ana: +1 to a gateway but cost of maintaining parity is real. How do we keep telemetry consistent across both surfaces?

jess: one option: canonical protobuf model inside service + automated JSON transcode layer for the gateway. Keep validation and contracts in proto, gateway just translates.

tom: downside is developer experience when making quick ad-hoc changes. If edits live in proto-first flow, console product folks can't easily iterate.

mike: could expose a stable admin REST surface for Console-team edits (CRUD), backed by internal gRPC for heavy ops. Essentially two tier: human-facing REST, operator-to-operator gRPC.

ana: That feels reasonable. For rollouts UX we also want real-time diff and safe canaries. Streaming updates to web client are required for live preview. How to implement?

jess: websocket subscription to a change feed from the gateway (or a small SSE endpoint) — simpler than browser gRPC. Backend still pushes change-events via internal stream.

mike: Agree SSE or ws is lighter. Implementation: service publishes change events to internal event bus; gateway subscribes and forwards to web clients.

tom: Telemetry: ensure every REST request from gateway includes upstream metadata: rule_id, rollout_id, operator_id. That way console metrics match internal traces. Use header: `X-Redwood-Rule` etc.

jess: Also add a response header with a short trace id for quick copy-paste from browser devtools. UX win for support.

ana: Quota accounting — do we centralize checks in the control-plane or push fast-path checks to edge services? Concerned about consistency vs latency.

mike: For strict quotas, central check w/ caching at edge. Async invalidation on change events. For soft quotas we can keep eventual consistency.

tom: Make sure console shows both the canonical value and the last-known cached value with age. Helps operators reason about staleness.

jess: Rollouts: need an API to create rollout groups + a fast way to rollback. That API should be idempotent and simple in REST. No reason to require a gRPC client for rollback.

mike: Implementation detail: expose rollback endpoint that triggers the internal gRPC action behind the scenes. Keep REST idempotent: `POST /rollouts/:id/rollback`.

ana: Sounds good. Any objections to protobuf-first with a small JSON gateway + SSE for console?

tom: one more thing: tests and contract tooling — we should generate both the gateway schema and a small OpenAPI doc from protos so Console E2E tests can mock easily.

jess: agreed. Also add a lightweight playground page that hits the REST gateway so product can try changes without needing CLI.

deploy-bot: deploy status: control-plane-pr-512 merged to staging at 2024-06-05T15:40:12Z :rocket:

ana: thanks all — I'll draft a short RFC: proto-first control-plane, lightweight REST gateway for Console, SSE/WS for live updates, caching at edge, consistent telemetry headers, OpenAPI from protos. Will share link when ready. :+1:
